lines: {target}? Sound travels farther than sense.
If anyone heads for Deep Dark, this is my advice. Walk soft and do not open every chest.
Sculk hears what pride forgets.
Deep Dark is no small story.
I will remember Deep Dark as darkness that listens back.
Before a trip to Deep Dark, someone at home should know my route.
I would rather carry a careful pack than a proud one into Deep Dark.
The peaceful parts would not lower my guard around Deep Dark.
I would leave the treasure behind before leaving a friend at Deep Dark.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at Deep Dark.
The part about sculk shriekers turning repeated noise into a deadly warning is enough reason to wrap every loose piece of iron.
There is no good time for a handle to split, especially around a drop hidden beyond the torchlight.
If something moving beyond the light showed up, I wouldn't want a cracked handle between me and the torch line leading upward.
No repair at a chamber with one clear entrance starts until everyone knows how to reach the torch line leading upward.
There is enough to watch on the deep passages under Deep Dark without carrying a rattling bundle of iron.
Something damaged at Deep Dark will probably change how I fit the next set.
The return from Deep Dark feels longer when a snapped handle leaves the iron useless.
If you left for Deep Dark tomorrow, would you choose the same gear?
At Deep Dark, one bent pick can be fixed. A whole pack lost to carelessness cannot.
I would like to see what Deep Dark did to the edge you carried.
{target}? Stone teeth hang above and wait below.
If anyone heads for Dripstone Caves, this is my advice. Look up as often as you look down.
Pointed stone makes every stumble serious.
Dripstone Caves is no small story.
I will remember Dripstone Caves as a cave that bites from both directions.
I would not leave for Dripstone Caves until someone knew where I was headed.
My pack for Dripstone Caves would hold food, light, and nothing chosen for pride.
The silence around Dripstone Caves would make me check the path twice.
Nothing found at Dripstone Caves matters more than bringing everyone home.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at Dripstone Caves.
I would not ignore pointed stone waiting both overhead and underfoot. Better to choose a repair spot away from dripstone.
Tell me we are going to Dripstone Caves and I'll start with a pick used without shaking the ceiling.
I would keep some strength in reserve in case of something moving beyond the light, even if the way ahead seemed quiet.
Cave darkness is no place to balance a loose rivet on one knee.
I'd shorten every loose strap before stepping onto the dripstone passages under Dripstone Caves.
Did your time at Dripstone Caves change which tools you trust?
I would choose a tight grip over a perfect edge for work around Dripstone Caves.
When Dripstone Caves was behind you, which piece of gear was in the worst shape?
There is room in my pack for a spare grip if the road leads to Dripstone Caves.
If the route through Dripstone Caves climbs, I lash every tool to the pack.
{target}? Pretty caves still have long drops.
If anyone heads for Lush Caves, this is my advice. Watch the vines and the holes between them.
Glow berries light paths that may not be safe.
Lush Caves is no small story.
I will remember Lush Caves as a cave trying very hard to look harmless.
I would tell someone the plan before taking one step toward Lush Caves.
For Lush Caves, I would choose food and torches before anything impressive.
I would treat the quiet parts seriously around Lush Caves.
The best account of Lush Caves ends with everyone back in the village.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at Lush Caves.
The part about moss and clay hiding water beneath hanging vines is enough reason to keep the path visible through the greenery.
At Lush Caves, a hoe for moss and shears for vines could save a long walk back with broken gear.
There is no good time for a handle to split, especially around a drop hidden beyond the torchlight.
If cave darkness came early, I would pack the tools and keep moving.
There is enough to watch on the lush passages under Lush Caves without carrying a rattling bundle of iron.
Bring me the edge you carried through Lush Caves and let me read the wear.
At Lush Caves, the best field repair is the one you prepared before leaving the bench.
Which failure at Lush Caves changed your mind about the kit you carried?
For another trip to Lush Caves, good equipment should make hard work possible, not make foolish work safe.
A keen tool is useful at Lush Caves. A loose handle makes it useless fast.
